html:
SMTO-EXE-0055 — The computer refused to start that app

GUID: 30c8aab0-ea05-5baa-af04-63a1e6e614f8
Slug: desktop-launch-failed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: desktop

What happened

  • SMTO found the app on the Gateway computer, but the computer wouldn't start it. The file may not be a program that can run, or the system blocked it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the Gateway computer to see whether the app opened anyway. If it did, don't ask SMTO to start it again. Starting it twice could open a second copy.
  2. Make sure the location points to the program itself, such as an .exe file on Windows or an .app on a Mac, not a document or shortcut. SMTO only starts programs directly; documents and shortcuts are rejected.
  3. On Linux or a Mac, ask the person who manages that computer to confirm the file is allowed to run and isn't blocked by security settings. The system refuses to start files that aren't marked as runnable or that its security checks block.
  4. Ask SMTO to open the app again. Once the location and permissions are right, the launch can go ahead.

What success looks like

  • The app opens once on that computer and SMTO reports it as started.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer. Don't turn off the computer's app security checks to force the app to start.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Desktop launch_application was rejected: the target is not executable or not an allowed type (e.g. not an .exe on Windows), the OS failed to spawn it, or the macOS launch/open call returned no application.

What this means

  • Launch preflight rejected a nonexecutable or unsupported file type, or the macOS launch completion supplied no application. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • Launch preflight rejected a nonexecutable or unsupported file type, or the macOS launch completion supplied no application.

How to diagnose it

  • Check target-local executable access/type and retained launch result; do not repeatedly launch merely because no window appeared.

How to fix it

  • Verify the path on the Gateway host is a regular file with execute permission for the Gateway account (an .exe on Windows), or a valid .app bundle with a bundle identifier on macOS, and check Gatekeeper, AppLocker or similar policy. Check desktop.applications for an already-started process before launching again, to avoid duplicates.
  • Check that the selected application exists, is executable and is allowed by the OS.

Retry and execution caution

  • Check that the selected application exists, is executable and is allowed by the OS.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended application has a confirmed process/launch result without duplicate launches.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass identity protection or automatically replay an uncertain mutation.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
